findings.evidence: Lines 384–389 explicitly call surjectivity one half and openness the other, while grep finds no `isOpenMap_rationalEvalHom` or `IsOpenQuotientMap` theorem for this map; lines 444–451 prove finite type through the generic surjective constructor instead.
findings.fix: Add `isOpenMap_rationalEvalHom` and preferably `isOpenQuotientMap_rationalEvalHom` under these hypotheses, using `IsTateRing.isOpenMap`, `continuous_rationalEvalHom`, and `surjective_rationalEvalHom`, then use the bundled result to build the finite-type witness.
findings.issue: `surjective_rationalEvalHom` exposes only surjectivity, although the documented presentation also requires openness; `isStrictlyTopologicallyFiniteType_toCompletionLoc` merely hides some open quotient behind an existential and does not characterize `rationalEvalHom` itself.

summary: The new evaluation presentation omits its bundled open-quotient API, leaving consumers unable to use the canonical presenting map directly.
